svg.text: What each relaxation metric measures, and how it drives the tree
Hz (γ stops at 45 Hz to stay clear of 50 Hz mains)
2 THE EIGHT METRICS (keys 1–8 in the HUD)
Relaxed vs. engaged: alpha grows and beta falls as effort and tension drop.
Simple and intuitive; closing the eyes alone boosts alpha strongly.
Relaxation deepening toward meditation: calm alpha and slow theta over beta.
Classic alpha–theta neurofeedback ratio; also rises if the user gets drowsy.
Share of all EEG power that is alpha; ignores overall amplitude (contact, gain).
Blinks and movement add delta to the total and pull it down.
Calm but awake: rewards alpha, penalises both tension (β) and drowsiness (θ).
Strictest score; use when falling asleep must not count as relaxing.
Middle ground between 1 and 2: theta counts half, so drowsiness helps less.
The 0.5 weighting is a heuristic, not a published standard.
Frontal-midline theta: marker of sustained inward attention (focused meditation).
Absolute power at one electrode, not a ratio: sensitive to contact quality.
Shift from relaxed wakefulness toward sleep onset or very deep meditation.
Cannot tell deep meditation from dozing off; best as a drowsiness monitor.
Classic attention marker (high = low alert arousal), used in ADHD neurofeedback.
Not meditation-specific; mixes relaxation with inattention.
Smoothed over 1.5 s and blended over 0.75 s when switching metric, so the tree never jumps.
Only relative values count. Absolute ratios differ between people, sessions and electrode contact; that is why every
metric is z-scored against the participant's own baseline.
Artifacts mimic states. Eyes closed → α up. Blinks or head movement → δ up. Jaw clench or frown → β and γ up (looks
like tension). Poor contact → flat line or 50 Hz hum.
Picking a metric. Start with 2, (α+θ)/β. Switch to 4 if participants drift off to sleep, or to 6 for focused-attention
